correctness.rationale: The displayed polynomial factors as claimed by applying the cubic root-of-unity product identity twice. The independent determinant expansion by exponent buckets gives the histogram 36,28,81,72,3 at norms 0,1,3,9,27, so no new concurrence appears outside characteristic 3, including in characteristic 2. Recovering point incidences from the vanishing triples gives 9 quadruple points, 12 nodes and 60 flags. Conjugation fixes 4 components, 7 singular points and 12 branches; normalization minus the branch scheme plus the singular locus gives the asserted motivic classes over the base field, with the quadratic étale class retained. Point-count specialization and exponentiation give the zeta functions, and comparison with q²+q+1 gives exactly 2,4,7. In characteristic 3 the reduced equation gives four rational lines in general position. The toric quotient of the local normalization-unit gluing is described by the incidence graph with each edge oriented from line to point; its characters are integral cycles. Its rank is 28, trace 2 in the quadratic case, and the rank of conjugation minus identity modulo 2 is 44−32=12 by independent stacked incidence-matrix elimination. Integral involution normal form then gives (3,1,12) for trivial, sign and regular summands, respectively. The local nontoric dimensions are δ−(branches−1), giving 27 away from 3 and zero in characteristic 3. Over a finite field the connected unipotent group is smooth and split, and Lang's theorem gives the product of point counts with the toric quotient. No splitting of the full Picard group is needed.
residual_risks: Restricted to the fixed reduced plane model. The graph calculation does not determine the unipotent group law or arbitrary Hesse twists.

checked_sources: Independent determinant, flag and integral lattice-type reconstruction
Geisser and the published Hesse boundary graph and Tjurina comparisons
value.rationale: The reduced singular-fiber divisor of the classical Hesse model is a natural test object in every finite characteristic. Its integral nonsplit lattice, unlike a rational eigenspace count, distinguishes the norm-one factor from rank-two restriction-of-scalars factors and determines the torus up to isomorphism. The arithmetic normalization corrections retain nonrational branches, and the resulting plane-filling classification is a concrete consequence. The evidential value is strongest for the integral torus and exact descent jointly, not for recomputing the geometric basket.
residual_risks: No general result for other pencil models or twists, or full description of the additive gluing group, is obtained.
